page: Amazon Web Services r8id.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core, and includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also demonstrate strong performance in the top 25%. However, multi-core execution and memory bandwidth benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and large-block memory reads, fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, the hardware delivers strong text generation speeds of 270.93 tokens per second on small 135M models, but performance drops to a weak 8.73 tokens per second for medium 7B models, highlighting a clear limitation for larger local LLM inference tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8id.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for memory-bound workloads by pairing high-speed DDR5 memory with dedicated local NVMe storage on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The inclusion of local instance storage reduces the need for external block storage for temporary data. This configuration is highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, database operations, caching layers such as Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from high single-core performance and fast local storage.
